sub_scenario.family: travel recovery physiology versus high-stakes scheduling
sub_scenario.one_line: airline training captain: the one asterisk matches the pairing exactly

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the check-ride records and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The duty roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Positioning flights followed by rest days are a non-event.
Buffered positioning is free.
Completely free.
Someone new shadowed me in the training center this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the simulator sessions into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My one busted check element in nine years came the morning after a minimum-rest overnight positioning flight; the same profile flown two weeks later on full rest was textbook.
One busted element, one spacing signature.
A nine-year record with a single asterisk, and that is the asterisk.
Back-to-back simulator days on home rest are demanding but clean.
Density is fine on proper rest.
Density was never the issue.
I archived last cycle's notes on the duty roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The training department's own fatigue guidance flags evaluative duties inside twenty-four hours of overnight positioning.
Their guidance already names the hazard.
Names it; the scheduler just does not read it.
A vendor call about the check-ride records ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the training center checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the simulator sessions.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the duty roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The scheduling system keeps pairing my recurrent checks the morning after positioning red-eyes; three of my last four checks drew exactly that pairing.
The system serially recreates the asterisk conditions.
Serially and indifferently.
I sketched next week's plan for the simulator sessions before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the check-ride records updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Check performance records are permanent and reviewed at every command upgrade board.
The stakes attach to a permanent file.
Permanent is what makes this worth a fight.
I compared two options for the duty roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the training center handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
I filed a formal scheduling objection to morning-after-positioning check pairings, and the chief pilot wants the rationale. What does my record support?
